To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the upper 200 ft or so of the Parkman sandstone in the southwestern part of the Powder River basin were deposited by a delta system with a wave dominated, high destructive type of shoreline.
the Upper Cretaceous delta in southwestern Wyoming is a high-destructive wave-dominated type.
the upper 2,000 ft of the Cody-Parkman delta were deposited in a wave-dominated, highly-destructive type of system, and the lower 200 ft were deposited in a fluvial-estuarine delta-plain environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the origin of the pillow structures in the Cody and Parkman, (2) the origin of graded beds and their relation to the origin of the pillows, (3) the origin of sandstone bodies and their relation to deltaic processes, (4) the origin of carbonaceous muds in the delta-plain facies of the Parkman, (5) the origin of lignite beds, (6) the relation of the Cody-Parkman delta to the
the sedimentology of a delta that is similar to those of the modern Mississippi delta.

the following: (1) sedimentary environments and facies of a wave-dominated delta, (2) the role of ocean-bottom currents in the deposition of graded beds, and (3) the relationship of a delta plain to its source and to its prodelta slope.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Upper Cretaceous delta was prograding southward, that its source area was in the Idaho-Montana cordillera, and that the sediments were derived from a complex of source rocks.

the Cody-Parkman delta was a wave-dominated, highly destructive type of delta with a prodelta slope that dipped southeast, and that the Parkman Sandstones were deposited by strong wave and tidal currents.
the upper part of the Cody-Parkman delta was a wave-dominated, destructive-type delta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the upper 1,500 ft of the Cody Shales and the lower 200 ft of overlying Parkman are a composite of marine and non-marine sediments.
the Cody and the lower Parkman are marine and the upper Parkman is non-marine.
the Cody-Parkman delta was deposited in a wave-dominated, highly destructive deltaic environment with a low-gradient delta surface and low relief.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Parkman Sandstones are a good example of a deltaic sandstone that has a high degree of lateral continuity and is not as laterally continuous as many of the fluvial sandstones that have been drilled in the Powder River Basin.
the Upper Cretaceous Parkman delta was deposited on a low-relief, southeastward-prograding, wave-dominated, high destructive delta.
it is possible to use a combination of field and laboratory techniques to reconstruct the depositional environments of ancient sedimentary rocks.
